channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents lack succession path
item.description: The constitution grants power, but political appointments sideline vice presidents from presidential ambition.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Environmental agency confirms practice destroys economic trees and worsens climate change effects.

item.title: Tanzania teams reach football finals
item.description: Taifa Stars advanced to the AFCON knockout stage and Serengeti Boys reached the U17 final.

item.title: Ghana opens two new health compounds in Keta
item.description: The facilities at Seva and Tengeykope-Anyrawase were built in seven months and include outpatient departments and delivery rooms.

item.title: Central African Republic state firms owe 56 billion FCFA
item.description: A World Bank report reveals that public companies in the Central African Republic have accumulated a debt of 56 billion FCFA.

item.title: South Sudan plans 94km dyke for flood protection
item.description: The dyke will protect communities in Jonglei State from recurrent flooding while preserving access to water and livelihoods.

item.title: 4.9 magnitude earthquake recorded north of Marsa Matrouh
item.description: The National Research Institute of Astronomy and Geophysics recorded the tremor at a depth of 16.60 kilometers.

item.title: Tenerife striker De Miguel dies after collision
item.description: Jesus de Miguel, 30, collapsed after a clash with goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a Spanish second division match.

item.title: Algeria women's team nominated for African best team award
item.description: The Algerian women's national football team is among 10 nominees for the 2026 African Team of the Year award.

item.title: Ouattara discusses Francophonie with Macron
item.description: Ivory Coast President Alassane Ouattara met with French President Emmanuel Macron in Paris to discuss international cooperation and bilateral relations.

item.title: Comoros prisoner dies, another reportedly hospitalized
item.description: Athoumane Abdourahmane, convicted in the Naïcha M’Madi murder, died at the military health center.

item.title: US investors propose pineapple farms and winery in Liberia
item.description: A trade delegation from Maryland, USA, plans to invest in large-scale pineapple farms and a winery, aiming to create over 350 jobs.

item.title: 28 state assemblies approve state police bill
item.description: President Bola Tinubu will soon receive the State Police Bill for his assent after legislative approval from 28 state houses of assembly.

item.title: Sallieu Bah penalty moves Zorya to fifth
item.description: Sierra Leone international Sallieu Bah scored a 55th-minute penalty to give Zorya Luhansk a 1-0 win over Epitsentr.

item.title: Madagascar digital minister resigns
item.description: Mahefa Andriamampiadana leaves his post, with the minister of higher education taking interim charge.

item.title: Lawyers accuse Supreme Court members of crimes
item.description: A group of lawyers filed a criminal complaint against the former STJ president and two counselors.

item.title: Dolphins reach Road to BAL Elite 16
item.description: Botswana's first basketball club to advance after finishing Lusaka campaign with three wins.

item.title: Makhadzi held in Botswana over P500,000 dispute
item.description: South African musician's passport surrendered to deputy sheriff pending court hearing on November 5.

item.title: Tanzania deputy minister clarifies mine royalty collection
item.description: Mine licence holders cannot collect statutory charges from small-scale miners, says Deputy Minister Steven Kiruswa.

item.title: Winnie Byanyima to chair environment institute board
item.description: The UNAIDS Executive Director will lead the International Institute for Environment and Development from January 2027.

item.title: Russia and US intensify influence efforts in Madagascar
item.description: Both Moscow and Washington are increasing diplomatic and security engagement with Malagasy authorities.

item.title: Tanzania targets 50 per cent formal jobs by 2050
item.description: Government initiatives aim to boost women's participation in innovation and procurement, with 23.34bn/- awarded to women's groups.

item.title: Tunisia defence budget rises 12% to 5.6 billion dinars
item.description: Tunisia's national defence budget for 2027 will increase by 12% to 5.6 billion dinars, with investment spending up 15%.

item.title: Senegal police arrest two over theft of Belarusian delegation's camera
item.description: A driver from the Ministry of Health and a market vendor were detained after a Nikon camera was stolen from the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games hotel.

item.title: Nadia Massé coaches Algerian gymnastics
item.description: French-Algerian coach Nadia Massé has been developing Algerian gymnastics since 2018.

item.title: Sialubalo demands fair market stall allocation
item.description: Minister Sialubalo says Lusaka has over 14,000 market stalls available but only 405 are allocated.

item.title: Senegal hosts African and diasporic arts events
item.description: Dakar is a venue for November exhibitions and festivals exploring colonial violence and Black identities.

item.title: ASUU threatens strike over UniAbuja land allocation
item.description: The union says FCT Minister Nyesom Wike allocated university land to private individuals despite a court order.

item.title: US contractor admits passing secrets to Ethiopia
item.description: Abraham Teklu Lemma shared classified intelligence with Ethiopian officials for over two years.

item.title: Liberia tells IMO seafarers must not be war targets
item.description: Liberia's Maritime Commissioner Neto Zarzar Lighe, Sr. voiced concern over attacks in key shipping lanes.

item.title: Liberian importers petition legislature over shipping delays
item.description: Business owners face seven-month cargo delays and rising port fees, petitioning for intervention.

item.title: Autopsy reveals 86-year-old Kenyan woman died from stab wounds
item.description: Dorita Macharia suffered over 20 injuries, including deep cuts to her face and neck.

item.title: DR Congo women mark 26 years of UN Resolution 1325
item.description: More than 200 women from various groups gathered in Kinshasa to celebrate the anniversary of the UN resolution on women, peace, and security.

item.title: EU election mission gives Zambia 13 reforms
item.description: Government challenges report findings, stating they lack sufficient historical and institutional context.

item.title: DR Congo assembly suspends prepaid meter installation
item.description: Bandundu's provincial assembly halted the rollout of new electricity meters due to tensions.

item.title: CHADEMA memorial marks one year since election crisis deaths
item.description: The opposition party held a ceremony in Dar es Salaam to honor over 500 people killed during the 2025 election crisis.

item.title: Foreign MPs ask Tanzania to guarantee fair trial for Tundu Lissu
item.description: Lawmakers from six countries and the EU urged President Hassan to rule out the death penalty ahead of Friday's verdict.

item.title: Mozambique road diversion authorised for gold mining
item.description: The National Road Administration granted permission for a diversion near Mavonde to HS Mining.

item.title: Mauritius men adopt festive attire for Divali
item.description: Men's fashion for Divali 2026 features natural fabrics like linen and silk in rich colours and intricate embroidery.

item.title: TRNUC commission works to implement recommendations
item.description: The TRNUC Enforcement Commission is making significant efforts to fulfill the recommendations of the TRNUC report.

item.title: Benin wins four Africa Tourism Awards
item.description: The nation secured top honors including 'Tourist Destination of the Year' and 'Cultural Destination of the Year'.

item.title: Liberia and Japan sign 250 million yen food aid deal
item.description: The agreement will provide rice and support broader development objectives through sale proceeds.

item.title: Tunisia temperatures to rise to 25°C
item.description: Cloudy skies are forecast across most regions with light to moderate winds.

item.title: Central African Republic remains poor despite billions in aid
item.description: Researchers find a deep disconnect between the globalized economy and local subsistence living.

item.title: Kenyan judge Phoebe Okowa wins full nine-year ICJ term
item.description: Professor Phoebe Okowa secured the required majority votes in both the UN General Assembly and the Security Council.

item.title: Dangote launches Walvis Bay pipeline project
item.description: Namibia's fuel prices rise as the Dangote Namibia Tank Farm and Regional Pipeline Project officially opens.

item.title: Kyaggwe wins maiden Airtel Masaza Cup title
item.description: Kyaggwe defeated Gomba 1-0 in a closely contested final at Wankulukuku stadium.

item.title: DR Congo justice agents protest unpaid bonuses
item.description: Over 100 agents blocked roads and burned tires in Kinshasa demanding their permanent bonuses.

item.title: Beninese cultural space hosts Quebec artists
item.description: Le Monde de Sica in Cotonou welcomes 10 artists from Benin and Quebec for a residency focused on identity and eco-materials.

item.title: Niger PM signs cooperation deal with Haftar camp
item.description: Prime Minister Ali Mahamane Lamine Zeine visited Benghazi on November 2, 2026, to sign an accord with the Haftar camp.

item.title: Namibian corporate debt rises to N$219.3 billion
item.description: State-owned enterprises also saw their debt increase by N$469 million in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Germany grants Uganda €50 million for development
item.description: The funds will support water, electricity, agribusiness, and refugee communities.

item.title: NPP targets minister for exposing wrongdoing, says NDC
item.description: Fifi Kwetey claims the ruling party is retaliating against Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa for revealing alleged theft and abuse.

item.title: Kabesha: PPPs key to closing Zambia's infrastructure gap
item.description: Attorney General Mulilo Kabesha says Public-Private Partnerships are key to mobilising private sector investment.

item.title: Bamako health centers get solar power
item.description: Three community health centers in Bamako received solar installations on October 16, 2026, as part of a larger program.

item.title: Madagascar photography festival marks CERES anniversary
item.description: The SAR'nao Festival in Antananarivo celebrates 20 years of the CERES education program and contemporary art.

item.title: Madagascar grandmother sentenced to life for murder
item.description: The Anosy court sentenced Raissa's grandmother to life imprisonment with forced labor for her murder.

item.title: Ladies Makis win Madagascar's first Olympic medal
item.description: The Madagascar women's rugby sevens team secured the bronze medal at the JOJ Dakar 2026 by defeating the Czech Republic 26-10.

item.title: Khomotso Phahlane corruption trial delayed until November 9
item.description: Former acting police commissioner faces R54 million fraud and corruption charges linked to software procurement.

item.title: Eswatini rights body flags police recruitment issues
item.description: Hundreds of job seekers queue in harsh weather for limited police positions.

item.title: Court dismisses ESRIC officer's disciplinary challenge
item.description: Siphiwe Mdluli argued the HR manager's involvement in initiating and sanctioning disciplinary charges was unlawful.

item.title: Eswatini SMEs face extinction threat
item.description: Economist warns local businesses struggle against foreign competition and rising costs.

item.title: Cape Verde minister warns of child sexual violence
item.description: The minister also highlighted concerns over the upcoming November 15 presidential elections.

item.title: NBA confirms it follows US policy on Rwanda deal
item.description: The basketball league told US senators it will adjust its business ties based on American government actions.

item.title: Algeria sends troops to Niger
item.description: Algeria formalised military support for Niger on October 21 with a cooperation protocol and parliamentary approval for troop deployment.

item.title: Ghana Air Force evacuates injured immigration officer after Hamile blast
item.description: An explosion at Hamile killed three people and injured an immigration officer who is now being airlifted to Accra.

item.title: Burkina Faso launches public conferences on patriotism
item.description: Minister of Justice Edasso Rodrigue Bayala launched public talks on civics and patriotism across all 47 provinces.

item.title: Haiti army chief asks Benin for military training
item.description: Lieutenant-general Derby Guerrier seeks Benin's help to train Haitian officers to combat gangs.

item.title: Burkina Faso and Türkiye discuss expanding partnership
item.description: The Turkish ambassador highlighted cooperation in health, defense, and education during a celebration in Ouagadougou.

item.title: Simiso Simelane releases seven-track gospel album
item.description: The independent artist's new project, 'Springs of Life 2', aims to direct listeners to Christ as the ultimate source of spiritual fulfillment.

item.title: Senegal assembly rejects revised budget law
item.description: Lawmakers voted 109 to 20 to block the finance bill without a full debate on public spending.

item.title: Ghana arrests three in Lebanon cocaine bust
item.description: Authorities in Ghana apprehended a Syrian, a Tunisian, and a Lebanese national following a 46.7 kilogramme cocaine seizure in Beirut.

item.title: Boubacar Barry found dead after alleged kidnapping
item.description: The body of a Conakry businessman, allegedly abducted from his home, was returned to his family for burial.

item.title: Benin mini-stations sell fuel at higher price
item.description: Formalized kpayo sellers charge 850 FCFA per litre, 100 FCFA more than official stations.

item.title: Libya justice minister vows to improve justice system
item.description: Minister Khaled Al-Modeer met ministry branch heads in Sirte to discuss workflow challenges and solutions.

item.title: Côte d’Ivoire sets cotton prices for 2026-2027 season
item.description: The government announced 310 FCFA per kilogram for first-choice cotton and 285 FCFA for second-choice.

item.title: Guinea president calls elections for November 29 and December 20
item.description: President Mamadi Doumbouya decreed voter turnout for regional and senatorial polls, marking the final stage of general elections.

item.title: German ambassador discusses trade with Misrata Chamber
item.description: Libyan businesspeople aim for easier visa access and German expertise to boost economic ties.

item.title: Jean Malonga's first novel published after 50 years
item.description: The 1953 novel "Cœur d'Aryenne" by Jean Malonga is now available from Présence Africaine.

item.title: Angola's sovereign fund takes stake in credit bureau
item.description: The Fundo Soberano de Angola is now a shareholder in Bureau, a private credit information company.

item.title: Tunisia arrests student with 2kg cannabis
item.description: Jendouba authorities detained a 19-year-old from sub-Saharan Africa for alleged drug trafficking near schools.

item.title: Algerian parliament examines 2027 finance bill
item.description: National Assembly members reviewed the draft budget, proposing changes for citizens abroad.

item.title: Senegal MPs block finance law
item.description: Pastef lawmakers refused to vote for the revised finance law, impacting social projects and salaries.

item.title: Benin Senate has powers France's does not
item.description: Benin's upper house can suspend or withdraw political rights, a power absent in the French Senate.

item.title: Mourinho mourns Tenerife striker's death
item.description: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho called the on-pitch collision that killed Jesus de Miguel 'shocking' and 'sad'.

item.title: UNET demands student bus and canteen services in Chad
item.description: The University of N'Djamena's student union has given authorities 72 hours to restore services.

item.title: Adeer International targets $2bn in Egypt hospitality investments
item.description: Saudi Arabia's Sumou Holding Group forms alliance with Egyptian partners for hotel projects.

item.title: Spain to dismantle Ceuta migrant shelters
item.description: About 13,000 people have returned to Morocco following a migration crisis.

item.title: Mauritania and Spain discuss fishing waters cooperation
item.description: Fisheries minister Aïssata Lam met Spain's interior minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska to boost maritime surveillance.

item.title: UN mission begins withdrawal from Western Sahara
item.description: All 13 sites of the UN's Western Sahara mission will close as its chief meets Moroccan officials.

item.title: Mauritanian filmmaker honored at Zagora festival
item.description: Mohamed Ould Idoumou received recognition for his career in film production, writing, and directing.

item.title: China donates over 300 farm machines to Liberia
item.description: The equipment includes tractors, tillers, and harvesters to boost food production and reduce reliance on imports.

item.title: Burkina Faso soldiers train for farming careers
item.description: 93 military and forestry agents began a three-week course on November 3, 2026, in Ouagadougou and Bobo-Dioulasso.

item.title: Egypt plans local production of Samsung medical devices
item.description: Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar discussed manufacturing ultrasound and mobile X-ray units with Samsung Electronics in South Korea.

item.title: Cameroon party president stands by election boycott
item.description: Issa Tchiroma Bakary reaffirms National Salvation Front's decision not to contest polls despite party suspension.

item.title: Senegal's PM meets China's envoy over Dakar 2026 Youth Olympics
item.description: Prime Minister LO discussed the ongoing Youth Olympic Games with Gao Zhidan, China's special envoy and Olympic Committee president.

item.title: Johannesburg zoo investigates over 20 bird deaths at Zoo Lake
item.description: Veterinarians will conduct post-mortem examinations on selected carcasses to determine the cause of death for the waterbirds.

item.title: Guinea-Bissau prime minister highlights economic growth
item.description: Public debt reaches 76.9% of GDP, while fiscal pressure remains insufficient for state needs.

item.title: Ebola kills 5,103 in DR Congo
item.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo's health ministry reports 10,467 total cases and 980 patients currently hospitalized.

item.title: Maputo hosts population and development conference
item.description: The Ministry of Planning and Development and UNFPA are holding a high-level meeting on November 4-5.
